title: Rate-window slew and tenant handoff leading to cascading 429s during JWKS rotation
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Summary: On 2026-02-11 at ~03:40 UTC we observed a multi-region spike of 429 responses for a subset of tenants. Symptoms matched a throttling storm originating at the API gateway layer: sudden increase in per-tenant token rejections, elevated retry traffic, and downstream queue pressure. Impacted customers experienced transient failures for write-heavy routes for ~18 minutes before automated fallback loops reduced load. Scope: ~12 dedicated-tenant pools across two regions, ~2% of total request volume during the window, several high-priority customers saw elevated error rates and SLO violations. Initial mitigation: Gradual rollbacks of a recent JWKS cache TTL decrease were performed, burst-window smoothing was applied, and a short-lived global rate-window growth cap was temporarily disabled to relieve handoff contention. Hypothesis and root cause summary: A recent change to JWKS refresh timing reduced the JWK cache TTL for RSA key rotation checks (PR #6843). That change caused a synchronized JWKS refresh storm for tenants with queued long-running connections. Because the rate-window allocator uses a tenant lease handoff heuristic that assumes stable auth token validation latencies, the synchronized cache refresh temporarily inflated perceived request rates for specific tenants, causing the allocator to trigger tenant capacity handoffs and reassignments. Handing off tenants between shards briefly duplicated enforcement state (double-counting) during the handoff window, causing artificially low available quota slices and resulting in a cascade of 429s. Contributing factors: (1) JWKS TTL change enabled synchronized external fetches; (2) rate-window handoff path lacks idempotency and uses a best-effort reconciliation that permits double-counting during concurrent handoff; (3) our monitoring didn't alert on per-tenant enforcement-count deltas rapidly enough. Evidence: Grafana panels show grouped JWKS fetch spikes at 03:40 UTC, correlating with a simultaneous bump in enforcement_count_delta and 429 rate. Trace samples show cache-miss callers blocking on external JWKS fetch for ~350ms. Timeline highlights: 03:39:45 UTC - deploy of jwks-ttl reduction to 60s to speed rotation compliance (canary). 03:40:10 UTC - first JWKS fetch surge observed. 03:40:50 UTC - per-tenant enforcement_count_delta spikes, 429s increase. 03:42:00 UTC - automated rollback initiated for jwks-ttl change. 03:52:30 UTC - rate-window cap adjustments and manual smoothing applied. 03:58:00 UTC - 429 rate returned to baseline. Postmortem conclusion: Primary root cause is interaction between JWKS refresh timing and the rate-window tenant-handoff algorithm which allowed transient double-counting of enforcement state. Several mitigations are required (short-term fixes and longer-term hardening).
comments: 2026-02-11 04:05 UTC — Initial incident declared by oncall (Marcus Lee). Immediate rollback of jwks-ttl canary started; monitoring configured to watch per-tenant enforcement deltas.
2026-02-11 04:20 UTC — Rollback completed; 429s reduced but did not fully resolve due to lingering enforcement-state dupe; manual rate-window smoothing deferred additional handoffs.

2026-02-11 04:50 UTC — Post-incident sync: narrowed root cause to interaction between JWKS fetch pattern and handoff algorithm. Decided on priority follow-ups: make JWKS refresh jittered, add handoff idempotency, and add enforcement delta alerting.
2026-02-13 09:15 UTC — Design review with serving-runtime and auth teams. Agreed to land three incremental changes (listed under action_items) and to run a canary exercise against dedicated pools.
2026-02-20 15:40 UTC — Prototype for JWKS jittering merged to feature branch; integration tests added for handoff racecases. Initial QA in staging shows reduced simultaneous external fetches.
2026-02-27 11:00 UTC — Load test scheduled for 2026-03-03 to validate handoff idempotency under synthetic JWKS storms. Marcus assigned to coordinate test harness.
2026-03-01 16:30 UTC — This ticket updated to In Progress with owners for each action item; estimate set to 5 points.
action_items: Add randomized jitter to JWKS refresh schedule per-tenant (owner: Priya Nair, estimate: 2): implement jittered TTL bounded between 45-120s and ensure canary flags.
Make rate-window tenant handoff idempotent (owner: Marcus Lee, estimate: 3): add a two-phase commit for handoff state updates and guard against double-counting enforcement metrics.

Add high-cardinality alerting on enforcement_count_delta (owner: Chris Martinez, estimate: 1): create a Grafana alert and PagerDuty rule that triggers on sudden per-tenant enforcement deltas > 50 in 60s.
Run dedicated-pool canary under synthetic JWKS storms (owner: Marcus Lee, estimate: 1): validate without impacting production customers and document results.
Post-deploy runbook update (owner: Aisha Kaur, estimate: 1): document manual mitigation steps for similar JWKS-induced enforcement storms and include rollback checklist for jwks-ttl changes.
